name: make_9_lvl2

input.prompt:
Propose a retrosynthesis route to synthesize the molecule with SMILES Cc1nc2c(-c3ccc(Cl)cc3F)nc(N3CCOC(c4cnn(C5CC5)c4)C3)nc2c(=O)n1C. The route must have 16 reactions.

Here are some guidance to help you (the reactions are enumerated in the order that they must be applied): 1. The free morpholine secondary amine displaces the remaining chloride on the electron-poor fused pyrimidopyrimidinone by nucleophilic aromatic substitution. A heteroaryl C-N bond replaces C-Cl and joins the core and side-chain branches.

2. A Suzuki coupling joins the heterocyclic chloride and 4-chloro-2-fluorophenylboronic acid. A C-C bond is formed while the heterocyclic C-Cl and aryl C-B bonds are broken. The other heterocyclic chloride is retained for the final amination.

3. Phosphorus oxychloride converts two of the heterocyclic oxo positions to chlorides. Two C-O bonds are replaced by C-Cl bonds, leaving the N-methyl lactam carbonyl intact.

4. Methylamine opens the oxazine ring and cyclocondensation replaces its ring oxygen with N-methyl nitrogen, giving the fused pyrimidopyrimidine trione. Two C-N bonds replace the ring C-O bonds.

5. Acetic anhydride acylates the amino group of 5-aminoorotic acid and promotes cyclodehydration to the fused oxazine trione. The new ring contains the acetyl-derived carbon and methyl group; C-N and C-O bonds are formed while the carboxylic acid is consumed.

6. Acid removes the Boc carbamate from the morpholine nitrogen, releasing the free secondary amine. The N-C(=O) bond is cleaved and the Boc group is lost, while the N-cyclopropyl pyrazole is retained.

7. Copper-mediated N-cyclopropylation couples cyclopropylboronic acid with the pyrazole N-H. A pyrazole N-C bond replaces the cyclopropyl C-B bond; the morpholine nitrogen stays Boc protected.

8. Di-tert-butyl dicarbonate protects the morpholine secondary amine as a Boc carbamate. An N-C(=O) bond forms while the pyrazole N-H remains available for the next transformation.

9. Hydrogenolysis removes the remaining benzyl protecting group from the morpholine nitrogen. Cleavage of its N-CH2Ph bond gives the secondary amine. The patent performs both debenzylations together; this route represents them as two template applications.

10. Hydrogenolysis removes the benzyl protecting group from the pyrazole nitrogen. The pyrazole N-CH2Ph bond is cleaved to restore N-H; the morpholine nitrogen remains benzyl protected in this explicit intermediate.

11. Acid-promoted cyclodehydration of the amino diol closes the six-membered morpholine ring. An intramolecular C-O bond forms with loss of water, converting the two alcohol groups into a cyclic ether.

12. Borohydride reduction converts the ketone into a secondary alcohol. The carbonyl C=O bond becomes C-O, giving the amino diol needed for morpholine formation.

13. 2-(Benzylamino)ethanol displaces bromide from the alpha-bromoketone by nucleophilic substitution. A C-N bond replaces C-Br to give a tertiary amino ketone bearing a pendant alcohol.

14. N-Bromosuccinimide converts the ethoxyvinyl group to an alpha-bromoketone under hydrolytic conditions. The enol ether becomes a ketone, a C-Br bond forms at the terminal carbon, and the ethoxy group is removed.

15. A Stille coupling of the bromopyrazole with tributyl(1-ethoxyvinyl)tin installs an ethoxyvinyl substituent. A C-C bond forms while the pyrazole C-Br and vinyl C-Sn bonds break.

16. Benzyl bromide protects the pyrazole nitrogen by N-alkylation. A pyrazole N-CH2 bond forms and the benzylic C-Br bond breaks; the bromine attached to the pyrazole carbon remains available for coupling.. Note that each of the hint describes the forward reactions for each step (enumerated in the order that they should be applied), but you have to perform the retrosynthetic reactions.
